findings.scenario: Segment is validated (checks passed, no reservation yet). User requests a different provider/model/effort. Switch rule 3 requires validated->cancelled, reservation no-op, then a new draft. The machine only allows validated->rejected|reserved|budget-exhausted. Line 340 refuses any unlisted transition and emits no provider call, so cancelled is dropped and the segment remains validated on the old route (switch stuck) or an implementer mutates the frozen route in place.
findings.remediation: Add validated->cancelled to the diagram and allowed-transition list; map pre-dispatch user switch to cancelled with no provider call; keep rejected for failed checks only; do not treat an unlisted transition as a silent no-op.

findings.scenario: Segment is reserved or queued with a live reservation and no attempt (attempt index 0 is claimed only at reserved|queued->active). User switch/interrupt must terminal as cancelled and release/reconcile the reservation. Failure-class evidence for user/system interrupt always requires a provider cancel observation (and late-output disposition). Driver cancel needs a fixtureAttemptHandle that does not exist yet, so a valid cancelled receipt cannot be emitted (reservation stuck) or the implementer fabricates a provider/driver cancel (illegal pre-dispatch call).
findings.remediation: Split interrupt evidence: pre-dispatch cancel requires interrupt intent plus reservation-release receipt only; post-dispatch cancel additionally requires driver/provider cancel observation and late-output disposition. Do not require provider observations when no attempt was claimed.

findings.scenario: maxAttempts is 1 while retryPolicyHash still describes the transient retry policy (validation does not reject that pair). Attempt 0 is retryable-failure with known billing. Retry rules test an undefined retry count is zero and never test maxAttempts. CAS text always allows claiming attempt index one. A second same-route fixture/provider call is issued despite maxAttempts=1.
findings.remediation: Fail validation unless (maxAttempts=1 and retry policy forbids retry) or (maxAttempts=2 and the one transient same-route policy). CAS may claim index one only when maxAttempts=2, attempt 0 is retryable-failure, billing is known, and billingState is not ambiguous. Replace retry count is zero with closed attemptIndex==0.
